title: Repeatable Load Anchors and RNG Control Protocol for Throughput Harness
content:
Purpose:
This note describes a lightweight protocol for maximizing repeatability in throughput benchmarking for our serving runtime. It focuses on the parts that consistently cause non-determinism or drift across runs: load generation RNG, priming/kv cache state, request ordering, and measurement windowing. The goal is not perfect determinism (that would be impossible end-to-end across heterogeneous hardware), but to reduce unexplained variance so that we can reliably detect regressions and quantify performance changes down to ~2–3% at target throughputs.

Background and motivation:
We've seen three common failure modes when trying to reproduce throughput numbers:
- Warmup differences: slightly different request ordering or priming sequences lead to different KV cache hit distributions.
- RNG and tokenization variability: non-fixed RNGs in client libraries produce different sampling for non-deterministic prompts (top-p, temp), changing request compute.
- Hidden state leakage: previous experiments leave stale artifacts on nodes (local caches, pinned kernels) that change perf.

Design principles:
- Anchor first, perturb later: create small deterministic "anchors" (short, repeatable sequences) that establish a known runtime state before the main load.
- Snapshot/restore as much state as practically possible: KV cache, model sharded offsets, and explicit batch sizing.
- Record provenance: every run must log seeds, config hash, and exact artifact versions (container image sha, model sha).
- Isolate noise sources: run a noise-characterization job regularly and use it to define acceptable variance thresholds.

Core protocol (high level):
1) Environment reset
   - Reboot nodes or restart serving processes to ensure a clean starting point for regression-critical runs.
   - Clear ephemeral caches on disk if present (local mmap caches, temp dirs).
2) Artifact pinning
   - Model artifact: use exact model sha (e.g. model:v1@sha256:...) and log it.
   - Runtime/container: log image sha and kernel driver version.
3) Load anchor step (priming anchors)
   - Run 3 short deterministic anchor sequences per node: 
     * Anchor A (cold): 16 requests of short prompts (~32 tokens) with temperature=0, deterministic sampling.
     * Anchor B (kv-fill): 8 long prompts (~512 tokens) meant to fill typical KV cache patterns for the target workload.
     * Anchor C (mixed): 32 requests with the actual target prompt mix but with RNG seeds fixed (see RNG section).
   - Each anchor run is single-threaded per client to avoid concurrency variation when establishing cache footprint.
   - Record timing and resulting KV cache hit/miss summary if runtime exposes it.
4) Checkpointing (optional but recommended)
   - After anchors, request a KV-cache snapshot from the runtime if supported. Save as checkpoint-<runid>-anchorA/B/C. This snapshot is used to restore state when rerunning experiments that must start from identical cache populations.

RNG and seed control:
- All loadgen clients must accept a --seed parameter that sets both the client RNG and any model-level sampling seeds (where supported). For sampling APIs that accept an explicit seed, pass the same seed. For APIs that do not expose a seed, wrap the prompt in a deterministic prefix that prevents model-side nondeterminism from changing compute profiles (e.g., fixed headers).
- Seed management: maintain a small registry of seeds per experiment series (e.g., seeds 1001..1020). Log the seed used in each client thread.
- Tokenization stability: pin tokenizer version and model vocab. Include tokenizer sha in run metadata.

Load generation configs (recommended defaults):
- Worker threads: match target concurrency but set per-client jitter to 0 for repeat runs. For variance exploration runs, enable jitter=5–15%.
- Inter-arrival distribution: use Poisson for production-like tests, but for repeatability baseline prefer fixed-rate (deterministic) arrivals for the primary regression runs.
- Sequence length mix: encode the exact distribution in the config (e.g., 60% short-32, 30% mid-128, 10% long-512). Save as explicit histogram.
- Batch calibration: run a pre-flight batched throughput step to discover the typical effective batch size, then fix batch size for the main measurement window.

Measurement windows and statistics:
- Discard the first N minutes/requests as warmup. We recommend discarding the first 180 seconds or first 2000 requests (whichever is larger) after anchors.
- Measurement window length: at least 10 minutes or until 100k tokens served, whichever completes first. Longer windows reduce variance.
- Use trimmed means: compute 5–95% trimmed mean for latency percentiles and mean throughput to reduce outlier impact. Also report standard deviation and coefficient of variation (CoV).
- Change detection: require a persistent delta for 2 independent runs before treating as a regression (e.g., two runs >2.5% lower throughput).

Repeatability checklist (pre-run):
- [ ] Confirm container and model shas are recorded.
- [ ] Run environment reset script (reboot or process restart).
- [ ] Execute anchor sequence and save checkpoint(s).
- [ ] Start noise-characterization job and confirm baseline CoV < expected (documented per-hardware).
- [ ] Lock loadgen seed and config file hash.
- [ ] Kick off main run with measurement window and recording enabled.

Repro scenarios and quick recipes:
- Reproduce a past run exactly: restore KV-cache checkpoint (anchor C recommended), pin seed, pin config hash, run fixed-rate arrivals, and re-run measurement window.
- Compare two models: run anchors between models to equilibrate kernel/kernel cache effects, then run paired fixed-rate windows back-to-back on the same nodes. Use the same seeds and batch sizes.
- Noise study: toggled jitter and arrival distributions across 10 repeats to characterize how much each knob increases variance.

Example candidate loadgen snippet (YAML-ish, plain text):
---
run_name: throughp-run-2026-02-01
model: gpt-open-7b@sha256:abcd1234
container_sha: sha256:deadbeef
seed: 1017
anchors: [cold, kv-fill, mixed]
arrival: fixed_rate
rate_rps: 1200
worker_threads: 24
batch_max_tokens: 2048
prompt_histogram: {short32: 0.6, mid128: 0.3, long512: 0.1}
warmup_discard: {time_s: 180, min_requests: 2000}
measure_window_s: 600
trimmed_mean: {low_pct: 5, high_pct: 95}
---
(When committing, save the full YAML as run-config-<id>.yaml and index with the run metadata.)

Common gotchas and troubleshooting notes:
- If two runs differ despite following the protocol, check: kernel driver changes, background cron jobs on nodes, and transient network issues to artifact stores.
- On multi-tenant Dedicated pools, ensure isolation: dedicated runs should run on isolated pools or use cgroup/cpuset enforcement.
- If KV-cache snapshotting isn't strictly repeatable across model versions (internal sharding layout changes), prefer full anchor re-run rather than relying on snapshots.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we standardize a small universal anchor prompt set in repo (3 anchors) and require it for CI throughput checks? (pros: maximal repeatability; cons: risk of overfitting runtime optimizations to the anchor prompts.)
- Investigate fast in-memory checkpoint format for KV snapshotting to reduce restore time under 30s.
- Automate variance analysis: add a step that runs 5 quick repeats and auto-accepts or rejects runs based on historical CoV thresholds.

Appendix: quick reproducibility log format (single-line CSV friendly entry):
run_id,created_at,owner,model_sha,container_sha,seed,anchors_used,rate_rps,worker_threads,measure_s,throughput_tok_s,throughput_err_pct,coefficient_of_variation
Example: r-20260201-09,2026-02-01T09:12:00Z,Aisha,abcd1234,deadbeef,1017,[cold,kv-fill,mixed],1200,24,600,1.23M,1.9,0.028

Notes to self: prioritize a small implementation in bench repo that: (1) enforces seed plumbing end-to-end; (2) provides anchor runner and optional KV snapshot/restore; (3) emits the reproducibility log line to a golden bucket.

If this approach looks reasonable I'll prototype the anchor runner in bench/loadgen/anchors and add an RFC for CI gating.
